newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices ease sharply in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices ease sharply in week.

text.p: Wool prices eased significantly on the last day of selling at sales in Sydney, Melbourne and Femantle, Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
The eastern market indicator fell by 12 cents to 605 cents a kg clean while the western market indicator rose 13 cents to 572 a kg clean since the last sales in Fremantle two weeks ago.
A total of 77,403 bales were offered, of which the trade bought 89.5 percent. The pass-in rate was 10.5 percent.

The council said the sharp fall in prices at the end of the week confirmed previous comments by exporters that extreme price increases in the two preceding weeks were supply, rather than demand driven and so could not be sustained indefinitely.
Pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety said prices reacted to the upward surge of last week, initially stabilising and then falling relatively quickly on the final day of sale.

"The traditional easing in the level of business with China, which occurs each year prior to Chinese New Year, would also have had a negative effect on the market, particularly with China currently accounts said.
Wool International said its stockpile of unsold wool totalled 1,891,845 as at January 23.
In the futures market, a total of 102 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended January 23.
The February contract fell 23 cents to 704 cents a kg clean.
Open interest decreased by 47 contracts to close at 835.
Sales next week are in Sydney and Adelaide, with 72,500 bales rostered for sale.
